title: Blocks Made of All the Words

concept.title: A sliding window that moves in steps of one word
body: All the `k` words have the same length `L`. You look for the places in the text `s` where a block of `k * L` letters consists of **all the words, each used as often as it is listed, in any order**. A block is just a sequence of `k` chunks of length `L`, so compare **counts of words**: a map `need` has the number of copies of each word, and a map `have` the counts inside the current window.

The start position of a block can be any of the `L` offsets `0, 1, ..., L - 1`. For each offset, cut the text into chunks of length `L` starting at that offset, and slide a window over the chunks: add the next chunk on the right; if it is a listed word, count it, and while its count exceeds `need`, drop chunks from the left; if it is not a listed word, throw everything away and restart after it.
Every chunk enters and leaves a window once per offset, so the work is O(n * L) chunk operations instead of testing all `n` start positions with `k` chunk comparisons each.

statement: You are given a text `s` and `k` words that all have the same length. Find all positions `i` (counting from 0) such that the block of `s` that starts at `i` and has the length of all words together is the concatenation of all `k` words, each word used exactly as many times as it is listed, in any order. Print the number of positions and then the positions in increasing order.
inputFormat: The first line has the text `s`.
The third line has the `k` words.
outputFormat: The first line: the number of positions.
The second line: the positions in increasing order (an empty line if there are none).
constraints: All words have the same length between 1 and 8, and k * length <= length of s.
The text and the words contain lowercase letters.

examples.note: The blocks barfoo (position 0) and foobar (position 9) are made of foo and bar.

hints: A block is a sequence of chunks of the word length; compare the counts of words with a map.
Try every start offset between 0 and L - 1 and move a window of chunks in steps of L.
When a chunk is not a listed word, or a word is used too often, move the left end of the window.

explanation: For every offset the text is cut into chunks of the word length and a window of chunks is slid along; maps of word counts decide when a window holds exactly the listed words.
solution.complexity: Time O(n * L) on average, space O(k).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

s = input().strip()
k = int(input())
w = input().split()

n = len(s)
L = len(w[0])
need = {}
for word in w:
    need[word] = need.get(word, 0) + 1
result = []
for off in range(L):
    left = off
    count = 0
    have = {}
    for right in range(off, n - L + 1, L):
        word = s[right:right + L]
        if word in need:
            have[word] = have.get(word, 0) + 1
            count += 1
            while have[word] > need[word]:
                have[s[left:left + L]] -= 1
                left += L
                count -= 1
            if count == k:
                result.append(left)
                have[s[left:left + L]] -= 1
                left += L
                count -= 1
        else:
            have = {}
            count = 0
            left = right + L
result.sort()
print(len(result))
print(*result)
